title: Quarantine-and-stitch mitigator + progressive rollback CI adapter
author: Aisha Kline
release_notes: Adds quarantine-and-stitch flow for isolating failing prompt subsets and a progressive rollback CI adapter to automate safe rollbacks during staged releases.
description:
Motivation: noisy prompt-set regressions frequently trigger coarse rollbacks or noisy alerts that hide actionable example-level failures. This PR implements a quarantine mitigator that isolates minimal failing example subsets and a conservative 'stitch' reintroduction workflow. It also adds a progressive rollback CI adapter to pause or reverse staged rollouts when quality signals degrade. Design: quarantine markings are added as optional metadata on eval result protos (additive, idempotent). The mitigator computes a minimal failure frontier using a greedy set-cover heuristic to produce a compact quarantine set. The stitch worker samples quarantined examples, runs targeted A/B smoke checks between candidate and baseline, and computes per-example recovery deltas. Stitch reintroduction rate is configurable (default 2%/hour) and guarded by a token-bucket rate limiter. The CI adapter watches sliding windows of quality signals (default window=3) and applies rollout fraction patches via the CI decision API with configurable tolerance and max rollback step. Checklist: - Implement quarantine mitigator core logic (greedy frontier selector) - Add stitch reintroduction worker and prioritized sampler - Add progressive rollback CI adapter and CI hook - Emit telemetry: eval.quarantine.count, eval.quarantine.ratio, eval.stitch.reintro.rate, eval.stitch.success.rate - Unit tests for mitigator and stitch worker - E2E smoke test in CI matrix - Operator docs and runbook - Feature-gate behind "quarantine_stitch_v1" and additive proto change
Testing: local unit tests tests/test_quarantine.py and tests/test_stitch_worker.py cover edge cases (empty sets, identical scores, concurrent quarantines). E2E smoke added to CI matrix using a synthetic prompt set to exercise quarantine->stitch->reintro loop. Performance: mitigator greedy pass benchmarks to <2s on 100k synthetic prompts in CI. Rollout: feature-flagged, staged rollout to internal staging, then opt-in for beta customers. Observability: new metrics and logs to correlate rollback actions with regression signals. Related: complements cohort-based gating and semantic anchors (see ENG-1972). The change is conservative and opt-in; the stitch worker is intentionally cautious and requires explicit opt-in in release pipelines.
